# `react/no-ref-in-render`

**A ref's current value is not read or written during render**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-react` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-react` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (moving the access into an effect or an event handler changes when it runs) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-react-hooks/refs`, `@eslint-react/refs` |

## What it checks

A component or hook doesn't read or write `ref.current` in its own body, for a ref made by
`useRef` in that body. Reads and writes in effects, event handlers and other callbacks are fine,
and so is the one lazy initialisation React documents: `if (ref.current === null) { ref.current
= … }` (or `== null`, `=== undefined`, `!ref.current`).

**Why:** React doesn't re-render when a ref changes, so a value read during render can be stale, and a write during render runs again — or not at all — when React renders a component more than once or throws a render away.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-react
pip install codelaw-rules-react
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:react/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:react/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"react/no-ref-in-render" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "react/no-ref-in-render" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"react/no-ref-in-render" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"react/no-ref-in-render" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"react/no-ref-in-render" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "react/no-ref-in-render": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore react/no-ref-in-render: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore react/no-ref-in-render expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule react/no-ref-in-render --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain react/no-ref-in-render       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule react/no-ref-in-render  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the read or write into an effect, an event handler or another callback.
2. If the value is shown on screen, keep it in state instead of a ref.
3. If the ref is created lazily, initialise it inside `if (ref.current === null) { … }`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function useLatest(value) {
  const ref = useRef(value);
  ref.current = value;
  return ref;
}
```

#### Do

```js
function useLatest(value) {
  const ref = useRef(value);
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    ref.current = value;
  });
  return ref;
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
function Counter() {
  const renders = useRef(0);
  renders.current += 1;
  return <p>{renders.current}</p>;
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
function Counter() {
  const renders = useRef(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    renders.current += 1;
  });
  return <button onClick={() => alert(renders.current)}>renders</button>;
}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
function useLatest<T>(value: T) {
  const ref = useRef(value);
  ref.current = value;
  return ref;
}
```

#### Do

```ts
function useStore() {
  const store = useRef<Store | null>(null);
  if (store.current === null) {
    store.current = createStore();
  }
  return store;
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
function Counter() {
  const renders = useRef(0);
  renders.current += 1;
  return <p>{renders.current}</p>;
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
function Counter() {
  const renders = useRef(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    renders.current += 1;
  });
  return <button onClick={() => alert(renders.current)}>renders</button>;
}
```

## Differences from the source

- Only refs made by `useRef` in the same function are checked; upstream also tracks refs passed in as props or returned by other hooks, and reports a ref passed to a function called during render.
- A second lazy initialisation of the same ref, which upstream reports, is not reported.
